----
========= ### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)
### quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip (priority 4)

**technique.** Class-conditional (Mondrian) cross-conformal prediction on the meta-model's nonconformity score, with the skip decision defined as 'win is not in the prediction set', a Mondrian taxonomy by class x time bin for the user's 'different for different time', and Adaptive Conformal Inference for drift in the live/walk-forward version.

**what_it_answers.** The user's acceptance criterion made formal: can SETUPs be skipped with a finite-sample guarantee that at most alpha of the true winners are skipped (marginally over SETUPs, under exchangeability), what skip rate, loser recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy each alpha buys on IS out-of-fold, whether the winner coverage holds on OOS, what the hour-of-day guarantee costs in sample size, and how far a coverage-chosen threshold sits from the expectancy-chosen threshold of the meta-label study.

**method.** Score s(x) = 1 - p_win_hat(x) taken from the meta-label study's IS out-of-fold probabilities (the scorecard variant, since the forest cannot live in the lab; the forest's scores are reported as reference). Cross-conformal / CV+ flavour: no separate calibration split is sacrificed (181 winners on 5m IS cannot afford one); within the harness's 12 purged folds, the conformal quantile is computed on the OOF scores of the winners in 11 folds and applied to the 12th, so the IS evaluation is itself out-of-fold. Mondrian by class: q_alpha = the ceil((n_win + 1)(1 - alpha))-th smallest OOF score among true winners; the prediction set contains 'win' iff s(x) <= q_alpha; gate = skip iff 'win' is not in the set, i.e. p_win_hat(x) < 1 - q_alpha. Guarantee: P(win in set | true winner) >= 1 - alpha, so at most alpha of winners are skipped in expectation; nothing is guaranteed for losers, their recall is measured. Alpha grid {0.05, 0.10, 0.15, 0.20, 0.30}; the smallest feasible alpha is 1/(n_win + 1) (0.0055 on 5m IS). Time taxonomy: class x time bin with three bins fixed in advance (09:15-10:29, 10:30-12:59, 13:00-15:19; the IS hour profile shows morning losses and afternoon gains); feasibility stated from winner counts per bin (5m IS: 16-39 winners per hour, so per-bin guarantees only for alpha >= 0.1; on 1m roughly 4-5x more). Robustness: |net|-weighted coverage (share of winners' gross net kept) reported next to count coverage, because the guarantee is per SETUP, not per rupee. Evaluation on IS-OOF per alpha: skip rate, winner coverage, loser recall, kept-vs-skipped expectancy and permutation p, control percentile (fz_report.random_control), top-decile-winner coverage; alpha chosen on IS by the pre-registered rule 'largest loser recall subject to winner coverage >= 0.9 and kept-vs-skipped difference > 0'. Exchangeability check: coverage per IS year and against the regime study's break tests. ACI variant (Gibbs and Candes): alpha_t+1 = alpha_t + gamma (alpha - err_t), gamma in {0.005, 0.01}, run sequentially over IS in time order, then continued into OOS from IS's final state without re-tuning, to see whether an online alpha keeps coverage under drift. OOS once: the frozen (alpha, taxonomy, thresholds) and the frozen ACI state, same table.

**leakage_controls.** Scores are out-of-fold from the purged, embargoed splitter; the conformal quantile uses only winners from calibration folds; alpha, the time bins and the selection rule are fixed before OOS; ACI's state carries forward without any OOS tuning; the study reads no OOS row until the single frozen run; the comparison with the expectancy-chosen tau is on IS-OOF only.

**compute.** Quantiles over <= 5k scores x 5 alphas x 12 folds and a sequential ACI loop over <= 5k rows: under 1 CPU-minute, under 100 MB; it depends only on the meta-label study's OOF file.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas; mapie is not installed and not needed (split/cross-conformal quantile and ACI are about 40 lines); fz_report.random_control / permutation_p read-only.

**output_as_config.** A "conformal" block in ST13/ST14: {"alpha": 0.10, "taxonomy": "class" or "class_x_timebin", "time_bins": [["09:15","10:29"],["10:30","12:59"],["13:00","15:19"]], "skip_if_score_below": s (per bin, the deployable scorecard's score at 1 - q_alpha), "calibration": {"n_winners": n, "is_window": "2021-10-01..2025-12-31", "oof_scores_sha": ...}, "aci": {"enabled": false or true, "gamma": 0.01, "alpha_state": a}}. The lab compares the scorecard score with a number; nothing else is code. Because the threshold is a single number per bin, it is the most compact form any gate in this study set can take.

**novelty.** Vovk, Gammerman and Shafer (2005) Algorithmic Learning in a Random World; Mondrian conformal prediction (Vovk 2012); cross-conformal (Vovk 2015) and CV+ / jackknife+ (Barber, Candes, Ramdas and Tibshirani 2021, Annals of Statistics); Angelopoulos and Bates (2021) A gentle introduction to conformal prediction; Gibbs and Candes (2021) Adaptive Conformal Inference under distribution shift, NeurIPS. Current because conformal sets on top of a meta-labelling model are the 2021-2025 way to turn 'skip only losers' into a coverage statement with a finite-sample guarantee; it is not in AFML but is the natural successor to its bet-sizing chapter.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: the guarantee is on winner count while P&L sits in the tail (a gate can keep 90% of winners and skip the three that made the year), exchangeability fails across the IS/OOS shift (5m -277 to -1,060), and the threshold it selects is the same number study 2 selects by expectancy, so it changes no trade. Fix: do not run as a study; report |net|-weighted coverage of the frozen gate as one row of study 2's OOS table; if a guarantee is ever wanted, weighted conformal on |net| with sessions as units.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: State the cross-conformal caveat: the OOF scores of the 11 calibration folds come from models that saw the 12th fold, so the finite-sample guarantee is the weaker CV+ / jackknife+ form (roughly 1 - 2 alpha), not 1 - alpha; report empirical OOF winner coverage per fold next to the nominal alpha. Merge with decision-making-4 into ONE operating-point step that reports both guarantees (winner coverage here, kept-loss risk there) on the same scorecard score, presents the Pareto front, and lets the user pick the point (Rule 0(c)); it is the same candidate as the scorecard for the OOS budget, not a second OOS look. Time-bin taxonomy only on 1m (5m has 16-39 winners per hour). Compute < 1 min.



========= ### decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control (priority 4)
### decision-making-4-selective-gate-conformal-risk-control (priority 4)

**technique.** Selective classification with a reject option and conformal risk control: a distribution-free finite-sample certificate on the loss of the kept trades, the winner-retained vs loser-avoided Pareto front, and cost-assumption sensitivity, to fix the gate's operating point

**what_it_answers.** Where to set the gate's threshold so that it "avoids only loss trades and not profitable ones" in a quantified, certified way: for a chosen coverage (share of SETUPs kept) what mean loss / loser share among kept trades can be guaranteed, how much winner-net is given up, and whether the chosen point survives slippage of 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side.

**method.** Score: the out-of-fold IS score from study 1 (E[net|x] or weighted P(win)). (i) Selective risk-coverage curves on IS CV: coverage c in [0.1, 1.0], selective risk = mean of clipped loss L = min(max(-net, 0), 6,000 INR) among kept, and separately the loser share; the curve is the decision surface the user chooses on. (ii) Conformal Risk Control (Angelopoulos, Bates, Candes, Jordan & Lei 2022): split IS by session blocks into train (for the score) and a calibration block (>= 200 sessions); for a target risk alpha, pick the largest coverage lambda whose calibration risk (with the +B/(n+1) correction, B = the clip) is <= alpha; the guarantee E[risk of kept] <= alpha holds under exchangeability of calibration units, which here are sessions (aggregate to session-level losses so weak dependence within a day does not break the units); report alpha in {800, 1,000, 1,200 INR} (the cost level: 1m mean cost 1,048-1,116 INR). (iii) Cost-aware operating point: utility U_w = sum kept net - w * sum over skipped of max(net, 0) for w in {0, 0.5, 1}; the Pareto front (winner-net retained %, loser-net avoided %) is presented and the user picks w (Rule 0(c): the operating point is a user decision, not a fit). (iv) Sensitivity: recompute every net at slippage 3 / 5 / 8 pts per side and with the brokerage cap at 20 vs 0.03% uncapped; the chosen point must keep a positive kept-minus-skipped difference at 8 pts. OOS once: realised selective risk vs the certified alpha (does the certificate hold?), kept share vs the planned coverage, kept/skipped expectancy, control percentile.

**leakage_controls.** Scores come from out-of-fold IS predictions only (never in-sample fits); the calibration block is disjoint in time from the score's training folds and sits after them with a 2-session embargo; the clip B and the risk definition are fixed above; w is chosen by the user on IS curves before OOS is opened; OOS is evaluated once at the frozen (lambda, w).

**compute.** Seconds to a few minutes: numpy sweeps over <= 5k rows, 2,000 control draws, four slippage variants.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (calibration utilities), matplotlib for the risk-coverage plot in the report

**output_as_config.** strategy_13/14.json "gate" additions: {"operating_point": {"coverage": lambda, "min_expected_net_inr": tau_at_lambda, "certified_risk_inr": alpha, "clip_inr": 6000, "calibration_sessions": n, "winner_weight_w": w}, "cost_assumptions": {"slippage_pts_per_side": 5, "survives_slippage_pts": 8}} with provenance. The certificate numbers are documentation of the guarantee, the two thresholds are the only trading numbers.

**novelty.** Chow 1970 (reject option) and Geifman & El-Yaniv 2017 (selective classification, risk-coverage) frame skip as abstention with a known zero cost; Angelopoulos et al. 2022 (Conformal Risk Control) and Bates et al. 2021 (RCPS) give the finite-sample guarantee that a plain threshold on a GBM score does not; the cost-aware utility follows the risk-sensitive decision literature (Rockafellar & Uryasev 2000 CVaR as the alternative risk if the user prefers tail control to mean loss). This is the study that turns the user's sentence about bands into a number with a guarantee attached.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: a certificate under session exchangeability that the 5m IS-to-OOS shift already violates; it sets a threshold on study 13's score, it is not a gate, and it would consume one of the three OOS slots for a re-parameterisation. Fix: the risk-coverage curve, the 3/5/8-pt slippage sensitivity, the brokerage-cap variant and the user-chosen w become one section of study 13's deliverable (Rule 0(c): the operating point is the user's decision on IS curves); drop the CRC certificate or footnote it with the exchangeability caveat.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Merge with quant-ml-canon-conformal-skip into one operating-point step on the same OOF score: report winner coverage (that study) and certified kept-loss risk (this one) on one Pareto front, and let the user pick w and the coverage on IS curves before OOS; one candidate, one OOS look. The calibration block of >= 200 sessions holds only ~110 sessions with a SETUP on 1m and fewer on 5m: state n as sessions-with-SETUPs and the resulting B/(n+1) slack, and drop the per-bin certificate on 5m. Keep the slippage 3/5/8 pts and brokerage-cap sensitivity as a mandatory harness go/no-go item for every gate (a marginal gate must survive 8 pts).



========= ### quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing (priority 5)
### quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing (priority 5)

**technique.** Probability calibration on purged out-of-fold predictions (isotonic and Platt, nested), expected-net sizing under the asymmetric payoff (Kelly fraction with class-conditional mean win and loss) discretised to 0-3 lots, compared with AFML's symmetric z-score sizing, judged with a lot-aware extension of the session-matched random control.

**what_it_answers.** Given a calibrated p_win and the asymmetric payoff (5m IS: 22% winners, win mean +10,878 INR, loss mean -3,429 INR, top-decile winners 46% of gross wins), how many lots per SETUP, whether sizing adds expectancy per lot beyond the skip decision, whether the calibration is real (reliability curve, Brier skill against the 22% base rate, ECE) on IS-OOF and once on OOS, and whether the honest answer with 181 winners is simply 'one lot or skip'.

**method.** Calibration: sklearn IsotonicRegression (and Platt via LogisticRegression as the low-variance alternative) fitted on the meta-label study's IS OOF p_hat against the L1 label, nested inside the harness splitter (fit on 11 folds' OOF, apply to the 12th); reliability curves in 5 quantile bins, Brier score and Brier skill score versus the base rate, expected calibration error, per model (scorecard is the deployable one). Conditional payoffs: W(x), L(x) = mean net of winners and of losers within calibrated-probability quintiles on the training folds; a HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile' (0.5) on |net| is tried only if the importance study shows any feature predicts magnitude (prior: it does not; say so). Expected net e(x) = p_hat W - (1 - p_hat) L. Sizing rules compared: (a) AFML 10.3 for reference: m = 2 Phi(z) - 1 with z = (p_hat - 0.5) / sqrt(p_hat (1 - p_hat)), which is wrong at a 22% base rate and is shown to be so; (b) Kelly fraction f = p_hat / L_bar - (1 - p_hat) / W_bar, half-Kelly, mapped to lots by fixed bins; (c) expected-net bins: lots = 0 if e(x) < 0, 1 if e(x) < c1, 2 if e(x) < c2, else 3, with (c1, c2) on a coarse grid (multiples of the median cost, about 1,100 INR) chosen inside folds; every (c1, c2) tried goes to the harness ledger. Book: lots x the intraday Foundation net with charges recomputed per lot via lab.trade_charges (brokerage cap per order matters) and slippage per lot. Judgement: net per lot, kept-vs-skipped per lot, maximum drawdown and per-session Sharpe of the sized book versus the 1-lot gated book versus raw Foundation; lot-aware control: extend fz_report.random_control so each draw assigns the study's own multiset of lot sizes per session to randomly chosen Foundation positions of that session (seeded the same way), giving the percentile and p_beat of the sized book; block-bootstrap confidence intervals from the harness. Sample-size statement: two cut points learned on about 180 winners on 5m give wide intervals; if the CPCV 5th percentile of net-per-lot improvement is not above zero, the study's recommendation is 'lots = 1 or skip' and the size block carries that verdict. OOS once with the frozen calibration map and bins.

**leakage_controls.** Calibration fitted on OOF predictions only and nested in the same purged, embargoed folds; W_bar, L_bar and the lot cut points from training folds only; no label information in x (as-of allowlist); the calibration map and bins are frozen with a sha before OOS; the lot-aware control uses the same seeding discipline as fz_report so the percentile reproduces; net per lot is the selection statistic so that adding lots to a few large winners cannot masquerade as skill without the control percentile agreeing.

**compute.** Isotonic and Platt fits: milliseconds; sizing grid of about 20 (c1, c2) pairs x 12 folds: seconds; lot-aware random control 2,000 draws x 1,026 sessions vectorised in numpy: under 1 minute; peak under 100 MB.

**libraries.** sklearn (IsotonicRegression, LogisticRegression, CalibratedClassifierCV with the harness splitter as cv iterable, HistGradientBoostingRegressor), numpy, pandas, scipy.stats.norm; lab.trade_charges and fz_report.random_control read-only.

**output_as_config.** A "size" block in ST13/ST14: {"lots_max": 3, "rule": "expected_net_bins", "expected_net_inr_bins": [0, c1, c2], "lots": [0, 1, 2, 3], "payoff_table": {"quintile_edges": [...], "win_mean_inr": [...], "loss_mean_inr": [...]}, "calibration": {"method": "isotonic", "knots": [[score, p], ...] at most 10}} with provenance; the isotonic map is a monotone step function so a knot table is a legitimate config, and the lab's position.lots becomes per-signal (it already prices charges per lot). If the verdict is 'one lot or skip', the block records that with the CPCV numbers that produced it.

**novelty.** AFML (2018) ch. 10 (bet sizing from predicted probabilities, sizing discretisation, averaging active bets); Kelly (1956); Zadrozny and Elkan (2002) isotonic calibration; Niculescu-Mizil and Caruana (2005); Guo et al. (2017) expected calibration error; the asymmetric-payoff correction to AFML 10.3 is the standard critique in the meta-labelling follow-ups (Joubert 2022; Meyer, Barziy and Joubert 2023, J. Financial Data Science). Current because calibrated-probability sizing with an explicit payoff table is how a meta-labelling model is turned into position size in 2020s practice, and because the lab already has the lot machinery to consume it.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 3 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Trap: two lot cut points learned on ~180 winners; the brokerage cap makes multi-lot cheaper per lot, a mechanical 'sizing works' effect; sizing multiplies whatever the gate got wrong on a book whose raw edge is negative. Fix: defer until a gate has passed OOS; then one table only, Platt not isotonic, charges per lot held at the 1-lot rate to remove the cap effect, and the answer is 'one lot or skip' or a 2-step monotone schedule; it never consumes an OOS candidate slot.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Sizing multiplies an edge that is not yet shown to exist (Kelly at the base rate is negative: 0.22/3429 - 0.78/10878 < 0) and per-signal lots is a lab code change the user has not approved. Fold into one conditional step merged with decision-making-5, run only after a gate passes the harness go/no-go with CPCV 5th-percentile kept expectancy > 0; default verdict 'one lot or skip' with the CPCV numbers. Keep the isotonic reliability curve and Brier skill as a diagnostic inside the meta-label study (seconds). The lot-aware random_control extension must be a scratchpad copy, never an edit of fz_report.



========= ### decision-making-5-kelly-bounded-sizing (priority 5)
### decision-making-5-kelly-bounded-sizing (priority 5)

**technique.** Position sizing as a Kelly-bounded policy: fractional / risk-constrained Kelly on the calibrated conditional edge, with estimation shrinkage from session-block bootstrap, mapped to a monotone lots-by-edge step function

**what_it_answers.** Whether, once a positive-conditional-edge region exists, sizing 1-3 lots by predicted edge improves log-growth and drawdown over flat sizing at the same average lots, and what the bounded, monotone lots schedule is; or, honestly, that the edge is not positive enough anywhere and the answer is 0 lots (the raw book has win rate 15% and mean -922 INR, i.e. negative Kelly).

**method.** Inputs: out-of-fold IS predictions from study 1 (E[net|x] plus 0.1/0.5/0.9 quantiles from HistGradientBoostingRegressor with loss='quantile'), realised net per SETUP, capital C = futures_margin 120,000 x 3 lots + 60,000 buffer (from the strategy files), per-lot charges from lab.trade_charges (brokerage cap makes cost slightly sublinear in lots). Bucket SETUPs by out-of-fold edge decile; per bucket estimate the return-on-capital distribution by stationary session-block bootstrap (2,000 draws) and compute the Kelly fraction f* = argmax E[log(1 + f R)] (scipy scalar optimisation; R = net per lot / C), the risk-constrained variant with a drawdown constraint P(drawdown > 20%) <= 0.1 (Busseti-Ryu-Boyd bound, 1-D per bucket), and the shrunk fraction f_s = 0.5 x the bootstrap 25th percentile of f*. Lots(bucket) = clip(floor(f_s x C / margin_per_lot), 0, 3), then enforced monotone non-decreasing in the edge bucket with <= 3 steps (isotonic step fit). Evaluate by replay with the lab's lock (one open position per contract) and 15:25 square-off on IS CV: terminal log-growth, max drawdown, Sharpe-like t on daily net, vs flat 1-lot, flat 3-lot and a lots-matched flat book (same total lots traded). OOS once with the frozen schedule; also report the schedule's value when study 1's gate is off (sizing on the raw book) to show it cannot rescue a negative edge.

**leakage_controls.** Edge estimates are out-of-fold IS predictions only; the schedule (buckets, steps) is frozen before OOS; the bootstrap is by session blocks so within-day dependence is kept; lots are capped at 3 and the schedule is monotone with <= 3 steps so the sizing rule cannot encode more than a coarse ordering of the edge; the sizing evaluation uses the same 15:25 cut and lock as the lab.

**compute.** < 2 CPU-min, < 200 MB (numpy/scipy on <= 5k rows x 2,000 draws).

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy.optimize, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (HistGradientBoostingRegressor quantile loss, IsotonicRegression)

**output_as_config.** strategy_13/14.json "position": {"lots": 3, "size_by_edge": [{"edge_min_inr": 0, "lots": 1}, {"edge_min_inr": 800, "lots": 2}, {"edge_min_inr": 2000, "lots": 3}], "kelly": {"fraction": 0.5, "capital_inr": 420000, "drawdown_cap": 0.2}} with provenance; "edge" is the same rule-list score study 1 ships, so no new feature is needed in the lab. If no bucket has f_s > 0 the block is omitted and the finding is recorded in S49.

**novelty.** Kelly 1956 and Thorp 2006 (growth-optimal sizing); MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2010 (fractional Kelly and its risk-growth trade-off); Busseti, Ryu & Boyd 2016 (risk-constrained Kelly gambling with a drawdown constraint as a convex problem); Baker & McHale 2013 (Kelly under parameter uncertainty, shrinkage). Sizing is treated as a policy downstream of a calibrated bandit value, not as a standalone optimisation, which is what keeps it from amplifying an overfit gate.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 3 · expected value 1 · keep False — fix: Trap: quantile regression of net on ~180 winners; Kelly on a book whose raw edge is negative returns 0 lots by construction, which the study already states; duplicate of study 5. Fix: do not run until a gate has passed OOS; then the one-table version of study 5 with charges per lot held at the 1-lot rate.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Duplicate of quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing on a book whose gated edge is not yet shown positive (raw Kelly is negative at 15-22% win rate). Merge the two into one conditional sizing step that runs only after a gate passes the harness go/no-go; ship the monotone <= 3-step lots schedule only if a bucket has CPCV 5th-percentile net-per-lot improvement > 0, else record 'lots = 1 or skip'. Per-signal lots is a lab change: ask the user before any key is written.

p=m["p"].to_numpy(float); s=1-p; blk=T.block[is_idx]; win=T.win[is_idx]; net=T.net[is_idx]
def mq(cal,a):
    cal=np.sort(cal); n=len(cal); k=math.ceil((n+1)*(1-a)); return math.inf if k>n else cal[k-1]
alpha=0.1; keep=np.zeros(len(is_idx),bool)
for f in range(12):
    te=blk==f; cal=s[(blk!=f)&win]; keep[te]=s[te]<=mq(cal,alpha)

# CRC lambda 0.1 on last 200 active sessions
act=T.active_sessions; cal_s=set(int(x) for x in act[-200:]); cr=np.isin(T.session[is_idx], list(cal_s))
thr=np.quantile(s[cr],0.1); kc=s[cr]<=thr; loss=np.minimum(np.maximum(-net[cr],0),6000)*kc
ses=T.session[is_idx][cr]; S=np.array(sorted(set(ses))); pos=np.searchsorted(S,ses)
ps=np.bincount(pos,weights=loss,minlength=len(S)); pn=np.bincount(pos,weights=kc.astype(float),minlength=len(S))
Rhat=np.where(pn>0,ps/np.maximum(pn,1),0).mean(); cert=(200*Rhat+6000)/201
pre=~cr; kp=s[pre]<=thr
print("CRC lam .1: n sessions",len(S),"R_hat",round(Rhat,2),"cert",round(cert,2),"(ledger 276.39 / 304.87); realised pre-block",round(np.minimum(np.maximum(-net[pre][kp],0),6000).mean(),2),"(1488.92)")
# how many controlled rows on 5minute have diff>0 AND control>=95 AND top1>0
rows=[r for r in H.read_ledger("operating_point",tf="5minute",label="L1") if r["control_pct"] is not None]
print("5m controlled rows with ctrl>=95:",sum(1 for r in rows if r["control_pct"]>=95),"of",len(rows),"; with ctrl>=95 & diff_top1>0 & sign>=8:",[(r["id"],r["sign_blocks"]) for r in rows if r["control_pct"]>=95 and (r["diff_top1_removed"] or -1)>0 and (r["sign_blocks"] or 0)>=8])
EOF

issues.what: The CRC step's attribution 'realised clipped risk before the block is 1.3-4x the certificate on every model: the exchangeability failure Judge 1 predicted' exceeds the evidence in two ways: (a) the CRC bound (Angelopoulos et al. 2022) requires the loss to be monotone in lambda, and the per-session clipped-risk R_hat is non-monotone in lambda on 5 of the 8 model x timeframe tables, so the 'certificate' there is not a CRC certificate and the excess cannot be attributed to exchangeability alone; (b) the ratio range is understated: actual 1.38x-4.88x (the agent's summary says 4.5x, FINDINGS says 4x).
